name: Global food prices
summary: FAO food price index 133.9 in October, below the 135 Alert line but up 5.9% on a year; next release 4 Dec
state: The FAO Food Price Index averaged 133.9 points in October, released on 6 Nov, down 1.2% on September but 5.9% above October 2025; the next release is due on 4 Dec (FAO). Sugar rose 6.6% on the month to its highest since December 2024, while cereals fell 4.5% (Food Ingredients First). The annual rise meets the Watch line and the index stays below 135; searches on 18 Nov found no staple export bans by several major exporters.
for_you: Households on tight budgets and import-dependent countries are most exposed to higher world food prices, which tend to reach supermarket shelves with a lag of several months.
rubric_hit: FAO FFPI 133.9 (Oct) in 120–135 Watch band; y/y +5.9% > +5% Watch line

sources.title: Food Ingredients First — FAO food prices October 2026

why: Food prices drive inflation, hunger and political unrest; poorer countries spend up to half of income on food.
drivers: Harvests, weather, fertiliser and energy costs, export bans, conflict in breadbaskets.

rubric.alert: FFPI > 135, or multiple major exporters ban exports of a staple.
rubric.watch: FFPI 120–135, or y/y > +5%, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: FAO Food Price Index < 120 and y/y change < +5%.
